question.text:
The formation of the oxide ion $\mathrm{O}^{2-}(\mathrm{g})$ requires first an exothermic and then an endothermic step as shown below $\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{e}^{-} \mathrm{O}^{-}(\mathrm{g}) \Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}=-142 \mathrm{kJmol}^{-1}$
$\mathrm{O}^{-}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{e}^{-} \mathrm{O}^{2-}(\mathrm{g}) \Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}=844 \mathrm{kJmol}^{-1}$

options.text: $\mathrm{O}^{-}$ion has comparatively larger size than oxygen atom
$\mathrm{O}^{-}$ion will tend to resist the addition of another electron

solution.text:
$$
\mathrm{O}^{-1}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{e} \longrightarrow \mathrm{O}^{-2}(\mathrm{~g})
$$
Due to the electronic repulsion, amount of the energy is needed to add electron
